_provenance: Vendored from the 2026-07-02 CLI E2E sweep (211 checks, 29 fails -> 21 regressions R01-R21). Spec: _SPECS/crewchief/research/maproom-cli-e2e-fix-spec.md. Runner: tests/e2e/run-fail-checks.sh executes one canonical probe per regression and maps back to these checks via the 'probe' field.
regressions: surface-exitcodes + sqlite-db-cache-migrate — `cache warm` panics on EVERY invocation including --help: exit 101, clap debug-assert "Command warm: Short option names must be unique for each argument, but '-q' is in use by both 'queries_file' and 'queries'" (clap_builder 4.5.57 debug_asserts.rs:112). Subcommand unreachable; exit 101 violates the 0/1/2 contract; implies debug assertions enabled in the shipped binary; supersedes known gap F69 (now unverifiable).

sqlite-db-cache-migrate — `migrate delete-backup` has zero table-name validation: '--backup chunks' DROPPED THE MAIN chunks TABLE with 'Backup deleted' exit 0 (sqlite3 then errors 'no such table: chunks'); nonexistent backup names also report success. Destructive data-loss footgun.

sqlite-db-cache-migrate — `db migrate` on the structurally damaged DB prints '✅ SQLite database is up to date' (exit 0) without detecting or repairing the missing chunks table; subsequent scan fails 'no such table: chunks'. DB unrecoverable except by deletion.

sqlite-db-cache-migrate — `migrate markdown --repo fixture` broken against the current schema: 'Error: no such table: file_contents' exit 1, after creating a backup table (partial side effect on failure).

sqlite-db-cache-migrate — `db cleanup-stale --confirm` claims 'Deleted: 1/1' but never removes the worktrees/repos rows; the same stale worktree is re-reported forever (SQLite only; the Postgres path converges).

sqlite-watch-incremental — watch never indexes uncommitted changes: every file event ends 'Tree SHA unchanged, skipping incremental update' because the gate compares HEAD^{tree}, which staged/unstaged edits never change — defeats the command's stated purpose.

sqlite-watch-incremental — phantom post-commit update: watch logs 'Incremental update complete files_processed=2' and emits update_complete while writing ZERO chunk/file/commit rows (verified via direct sqlite3 inspection; new symbols return 0 search hits). Same pattern on branch switch (new worktree stays chunk_count=0).

sqlite-watch-incremental — the phantom update advances index_state.tree_sha, poisoning subsequent incremental scans: '✓ No changes detected (tree SHA match), skipping scan' against a stale index; only `scan --force` recovers.

sqlite-core-scan-search + postgres-core — per-commit chunk accumulation on BOTH backends: a deleted function remains searchable with stale content after upsert AND --force rescan; SQLite chunks grew 10→20, PG chunk_worktrees inflated 10→15 with doubled language counts; no cleanup path (clean-ignored / cleanup-stale do not reclaim); only search-time dedup masks it.

postgres-core — `search --preview/--preview-length` is a silent no-op on the PG path: no preview field in JSON, agent format prints '-' placeholder, despite chunks.preview being populated in the DB and help promising implicit 120-char previews.
sqlite-core-scan-search — JSON search output lacks `total_estimate` (field is `total_matches`) while agent format prints 'total_estimate=3' for the same query — cross-format field-name inconsistency.
surface-exitcodes — empty `--database-url ""` silently accepted: exit 0 against an ephemeral SQLite DB, MAPROOM_DATABASE_URL ignored — silent data-destination loss instead of config-error exit 2.

embeddings-degraded + embeddings-real-google — exit-code contract broken for config errors: vector-search default json format exits 1 with a raw anyhow chain while --format agent exits 2 with a structured ERROR line for the identical error; the same missing-credentials condition exits 2 from generate-embeddings but 1 from vector-search and serve.

embeddings-degraded (confirmed by daemon-stdio-postgres and daemon-socket) — OLLAMA_URL / MAPROOM_OLLAMA_URL / OLLAMA_HOST are ignored: embedding endpoint hardcoded to http://localhost:11434 despite --help documenting OLLAMA_URL; the container's host ollama is unreachable by design.

embeddings-degraded — generate-embeddings prints fictional success stats ('Generated: 0, Cached: 20, API calls: 0, Tokens: 0, Cost: $0.0000, cache hit 100.0%') while real network calls provably occur (stopping the mock server makes the identical --force run fail with ConnectionRefused). Embeddings are written correctly.

embeddings-real-google + daemon-stdio-sqlite + daemon-stdio-postgres + daemon-socket — `serve` hard-requires embedding-service init before serving even FTS-only requests and exits 1 (not 2) on the resulting config error; socket mode mislabels it 'Database error'. With the container's default env (MAPROOM_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=google, no credentials) `maproom serve` is dead on arrival in all modes and on both backends — no graceful fallback like scan has.

daemon-stdio-sqlite + daemon-stdio-postgres — tracing logs written to STDOUT interleaved with JSON-RPC responses (ANSI-colored ERROR lines even at default log level; stderr 0 bytes). Root cause main.rs:1041 fmt().init() without .with_writer(stderr). Corrupts the newline-delimited protocol for strict clients; only workaround is RUST_LOG=off.

daemon-stdio-sqlite — unknown worktree name in search params is silently dropped (db/sqlite/mod.rs:1447 .optional() → None = no filter): returns byte-identical all-worktree results instead of error/empty — wrong-scope results in multi-worktree DBs.

daemon-stdio-sqlite + daemon-stdio-postgres — JSON-RPC 2.0 spec deviations: notifications (requests without id) receive {"result":...,"id":null} replies; the jsonrpc version field is never validated ('1.0' accepted; #[allow(dead_code)] in types.rs:6); batch arrays yield -32700 instead of batch handling/-32600.
daemon-socket — --idle-timeout 5 actually shuts down ~69s after last activity because the idle check polls on a ~60s tick; values under 60s are effectively rounded up to ~60-70s.
daemon-socket — the socket file is never unlinked on any shutdown path (SIGTERM or graceful idle; the PID file IS removed); stale .sock files accumulate, mitigated only by silent rebind on restart.

fail_checks.expected: --idle-timeout 5 exits within ~15s (proportional tick)
fail_checks.feature: --idle-timeout 5 (idle shutdown timing)
fail_checks.command: timeout 90 /tmp/maproom-sqlite serve --socket --socket-path $WORK/mr.sock --idle-timeout 5; one request, disconnect, poll for exit
fail_checks.evidence: Daemon exited 69s after last activity, not ~5s. Debug log shows the cause: idle check polls on a ~60s tick — 'DEBUG No active clients, idle timer started' at start+60s, then 'SIGTERM received, initiating graceful shutdown' 10s later; 'PID file removed'. It DOES self-terminate (before my 90s wrapper), but --idle-timeout values <60s are effectively rounded up to ~60-70s. Not in the known-gap list.

fail_checks.expected: socket file unlinked on SIGTERM and idle shutdown

fail_checks.evidence: Socket file is NEVER unlinked on shutdown — left stale after SIGTERM-kill AND after graceful idle shutdown (PID file is removed, socket is not). Mitigation works: a restarting daemon silently rebinds over the stale socket, so impact is hygiene-only (orphan .sock files accumulate). Minor, but asymmetric with PID-file cleanup.
